notes: ARCHITECTURAL ADHERENCE (6/10): The event bus is used correctly for task.assigned, task.status-changed, and comment.added events. However, NotificationService receives direct references to TaskService and UserService in its constructor and calls them directly (this.taskService.getTask(), this.userService.getUser()), which violates Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls). The notification service should only react to event payloads. The API Router correctly centralizes all HTTP handling. Services own their own data stores. COMPLETENESS (7/10): Core CRUD for all entities is present. Events for task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added are implemented. Demo script exercises the main flows. Missing: (1) Comment field is named 'text' in implementation but spec says 'body'; (2) Task field is named 'assignee' but spec says 'assigneeId'; (3) Project field is 'members' (array of IDs) but demo accesses 'members.length' expecting it to be enriched objects — the demo references 'finalProject.members.length' which works but is inconsistent with data model expectations; (4) No unsubscribe mechanism on EventBus; (5) updateTaskStatus allows same-status transition (newIndex === currentIndex), which is debatable but not clearly wrong; (6) No validation that assigneeId or projectId exist when creating/assigning tasks; (7) NotificationService comment handler truncates with '...' even for short comments (no length check before substring). CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE (5/10): Rule 1 violated — NotificationService directly imports and calls TaskService and UserService methods rather than relying solely on event payloads. This is the most significant violation. Rule 2 satisfied. Rule 3 satisfied. Rule 4 satisfied (forward-only transitions enforced). Rule 5 satisfied (only 'crypto' built-in used). Rule 6 satisfied (each service in its own file). CODE QUALITY (7/10): Generally clean TypeScript, good use of Maps, proper async/await, UUID generation, error handling in router. Issues: 'any' types used in event handlers; error catch uses 'error: any' in one place; the global singleton eventBus export creates implicit coupling; respondJSON return type is void but called with 'return' inconsistently mixing void/Promise<void>; no input sanitization; parseBody lacks size limits (potential DoS); the extractId method is fragile and relies on path manipulation rather than proper route parameter extraction; DELETE /projects/:id/members reads body which is non-standard (should use query param or path param).
